in_hebrew.name: אופיר
in_hebrew.meaning: עופיר הוא שם שמקורו במקרא ופירושו עושר או זהב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עופיר הוא שם שמקורו במקרא ופירושו עושר או זהב. השם עופיר מוזכר במקרא כבנו של שוע, אחד מלכי סבא, וכמקום ממנו באו זהב ואבנים יקרות. השם עופיר משמש גם כמטפורה לעושר ולגדולה.

in_greek.name: Ωφείρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ωφείρ σημαίνει πλούτος ή χρυσός. Το όνομα Ωφείρ αναφέρεται στην Αγία Γραφή ως γιος του Σουά, ενός από τους βασιλιάδες της Σάβα, και ως τόπος από τον οποίο προέρχονται χρυσός και πολύτιμες πέτρες. Το όνομα Ωφείρ χρησιμοποιείται επίσης ως μεταφορά για τον πλούτο και τη μεγαλοσύνη.

in_latin.name: Ophir
in_latin.long_meaning: Ophir means wealth or gold. The name Ophir is derived from the Hebrew Bible and refers to a son of Shuah, one of the kings of Saba, and to a place from which gold and precious stones come. The name Ophir is also used as a metaphor for wealth and greatness.

in_english.name: Ophir
in_english.meaning: Ophir means rich, wealthy, or golden
in_english.long_meaning: Ophir is a Christian name that originates from the Hebrew Bible, specifically from the book of Genesis. It refers to a son of Shuah, one of the kings of Saba, and to a place renowned for its gold and precious stones. The name Ophir symbolizes wealth, prosperity, and grandeur. In Christian tradition, Ophir is associated with riches, success, and spiritual abundance. The name has been used across various Christian cultures, reflecting its biblical roots and enduring significance.

biblical_reference.note: Ophir is mentioned as a son of Shuah, one of the kings of Saba.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ophir" has been associated with wealth and riches due to its biblical connection as a land famous for its gold and precious stones. It is a place of wonder and allure, inspiring endless quests and dreams of expanding one's wealth and possessions.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name "Ophir" may symbolize the spiritual pursuit of wealth and riches in the form of wisdom and enlightenment. In Christianity, this can be interpreted as the inner treasure of the soul, which is more valuable and enduring than any material possessions. Just as King Solomon sought wisdom above all else, Ophir as a spiritual ideal calls us to prioritize our quest for inner wisdom and understanding over the pursuit of external wealth and possessions. This can lead to a more fulfilling and meaningful life, as we recognize that true wealth lies not in material possessions but in the richness of our inner worlds.
